cases.customer_question: Can a module with LE transmit power below Class 1 be qualified by referencing a Controller design that is registered as LE Class 1:YES?
question_variants: Can I combine a Class 2 module with a Class 1 controller QDID?
LE Class 1 consistency issue in Controller Subsystem qualification
Why does RF PHY need Class 1:YES when the referenced controller is Class 1:YES?
Can a low-power LE module reuse a Class 1 controller design?
Bluetooth SIG inter-layer consistency error for LE Class 1
cases.actual_issue: The planned qualification reused a controller design whose LL declaration included LE Class 1:YES. The new module could only be combined with that design if its RF PHY qualification evidence also satisfied the corresponding LE Class 1 requirements.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG qualification requires consistency between capabilities declared in referenced designs and the tested product. If the reused controller design claims LE Class 1 support, the RF PHY evidence used with it must also be consistent with Class 1 operation. A lower-power implementation cannot simply reuse a higher-power controller declaration without creating a qualification inconsistency.
cases.consultant_answer: The referenced controller registration contained LL capability declarations indicating LE Class 1:YES. Therefore, the RF PHY qualification associated with the new module must also correspond to Class 1 operation. If the module transmits below the LE Class 1 range, the referenced controller design cannot be used as-is. The customer must either select a controller design already registered with LE Class 1:NO or obtain an updated controller registration reflecting the correct capability.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth qualification combinations must remain consistent across referenced layers. A controller design declaring LE Class 1:YES cannot be combined with RF PHY evidence that represents a non-Class-1 implementation without creating an inter-layer consistency failure.
cases.final_recommendation: Verify the module's actual LE transmit-power classification before selecting reusable controller designs. If the module is not LE Class 1, use a controller registration with LE Class 1:NO or request an updated component qualification from the component owner.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: The qualification combination may fail consistency validation and the registration process may not be completed. This can force redesign of the qualification strategy and create project delays.
